// diagnostic

E0140

`#SingleUse` value dropped without being consumed at scope end

What

`#SingleUse` value dropped without being consumed at scope end

Why

A `#SingleUse` value carries a job that must be done, so dropping it leaves that job undone

Fix

Consume the `#SingleUse` value before scope end.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0140: Tests/UI/Ownership/raw_window_read_after_its_owner_is_released.stderr.

Error [jet.OwnerMovedWhileViewed]: `cells` cannot be moved while `ints` is still looking into it
  --> Tests/UI/Ownership/raw_window_read_after_its_owner_is_released.jet:19:17
    |
 19 |         release(cells)
    |                 ^^^^^
 Why: `ints` is a live read view into `cells`; changing or moving the owner could invalidate that view
 Fix: Finish using `ints` before changing `cells`, narrow the view's scope, or make an owned copy
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0212

Error [jet.SingleUseDropped]: `cells` still owes `consume`
  --> Tests/UI/Ownership/raw_window_read_after_its_owner_is_released.jet:15:5
    |
 15 |     cells := Cells{a: 11, b: 22}
    |     ^^^^^
 Why: This value's type is `#SingleUse`, so it carries a job that has to be done — dropping it without doing that job leaves the work undone (an unjoined task, an unreleased lock)
 Fix: Consume it exactly once: pass it to a `&&` parameter, or `return` it — or write `#Unsafe("reason") { consume(cells) }` to discard it deliberately
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0140
